s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden onset of oral and skin lesions with abdominal discomfort and difficulty eating, accompanied by extensive papillomatosis and verrucous plaques
salient_findings: Sudden warty growths over the lips
Extensive papillomatosis over the lips, tongue, and palate
Verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in the axillae, posterior neck, periumbilical region, and groin folds
Ridged appearance and coarse texture of palms with papillomatous appearance
key_facts: 70-year-old woman
Sudden onset of oral lesions
Difficulty eating
6-month history of vague abdominal discomfort
Extensive papillomatosis over the lips, tongue, and palate
Verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in multiple areas
Ridged appearance and coarse texture of palms
Abdominal CT showed large left-sided renal mass with retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy
Thorax CT showed necrotic mediastinal lymphadenopathy causing superior vena cava compression
Biopsy of renal mass revealed invasive carcinoma with focal squamous differentiation

shortlist.label: Florid cutaneous papillomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of sudden onset of oral and skin lesions with papillomatosis

shortlist.label: Tylosis with oesophageal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation of oral lesions, although esophageal cancer is not mentioned, the renal mass could be a related cancer

shortlist.label: Howel-Evans syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by tylosis and esophageal cancer, which could be related to the patient's oral lesions and abdominal discomfort

shortlist.label: Urothelial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Confirmed by biopsy of the renal mass, which is a primary cancer that could be related to the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Papillomatosis cutis carcinoides
shortlist.why_kept: Rare condition that could explain the patient's skin and oral lesions, as well as the abdominal discomfort

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the patient's oral lesions and the biopsy results showing focal squamous differentiation

shortlist.label: Renal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the large left-sided renal mass, although the biopsy suggested urothelial carcinoma

shortlist.label: Gorlin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Rare genetic disorder that could explain the patient's skin and oral lesions, as well as the increased risk of cancer
